An ordinance for the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia regulating and establishing the location, placement, operation and development of mobile home parks within the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia; to define the words used in this ordinance; to provide for applications for mobile home parks; to provide minfmum number of mobile home spaces; to provide for the required lot area; ta provide for yard requirements; to provide for drainage, interior drives and walkways; to provide far off-drive parking; to provide for signs regarding park identification and mobile hame identification; to provide for requiations governing improvement to mohile homes; to provide for special conditions and safeguards; to provide for general requirements regarding minimum size of mobile homes, water, sawaqge, electricity, lighting, refuse collection facilities, recreation area, and service building; to provide for regulations regarding existing mobile home parks and individual mobile homes and conpliance with this resolution; to provide for development compliance of mobile hame parks; to provide for legal provisions regarding violation and penalties, separability provisions and conflict with other regulations; and to provide for an effective date of this ordinance.

BE IT ORDAINED by the Mayor and Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia and it is ordained by authority of said Mayor and Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia that-there is established by this ordinance rules and regulations for mobile home parks For Pine Mountain, Georgia; it is the intent of this Ordinance to establish minimum standards for the operation and development of mobile home parks and to prohibit the placement of individual mohiie homes not in an authorized mobile home park as herein specified within the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia. Mobile home parks shall be permitted in any area approved by the Mayor and Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia on the effective date of this Ordinance.

Shall have the meaning given in this section. Terms not herein defined shall have their customary dictionary definitions where not inconsistent with the context. The term "shall" is mandatory. - 1. Person - shell mean any individual, firm, trust, partnership, association, corporation or any other legal entity capable of owning real estate.

- 4. Mobile Home Space- A piot of ground within a Mobile Home Park designated for the accommodation of not more than one (1) mobile home of single family occupancy.

S. Mobile Home Park- A lot or parcel of Land which has been planned and improved for the placement of mobile homes for non-transient use.

. 6. Service Building- A building, housing facilities such as: recreational, maintenance, laundry and office structures necessary to the successful development and Management of a@ Mobile Home Park.

Mobile Homes on Individual Lots- It ghall he unlawful for any person to place a trailer or mobile home, whether permanent, dependent or independent, designed for use for human habitetion, and then use same for living, sleeping or business purposes on any premises in the Town of Pine Mountain except in authorized mobile home parks duly permitted and maintained pursuant to the provisions of this Ordinance. It shall be unlawful for any person to park, for use or accupancy, any mohile home or trailer as defined herein overnight on any street, alley, highway or other public place within the Town of Pine Mountain.

SECTION C: Dimensional and Site Development Requirements (Mobile Home Park Plan). The Mobile Park Plan shall show or propose all requirements listed in this Ordinance, and in addition, all Said requirements shail he complied with before a certificate of occupancy can be issued.

SECTION D: Minimum Number of Mobile Home Spaces. No park shall be permitted with less than Twenty (20) spaces.

SECTION E: Required Lot (Mobile Home Space} Area. Well de-fined mobile home spaces shail be provided, consisting of 2 minimum of four thousand five hundred (4,500) square feet for each Space.

SECTION F: Yard Requirements: Each space shall be at Least fifty (50) feet wide and clearly defined. There shall be at least a twenty (20) foot side yard and a fifteen (15) foot clearance between mobile homes including mobile homes parked end to end. No mobile home sheli be Located closer than fifteen (15) feet to any building or street within the park; within twenty (20) feet of any exterior street or boundary line of the park.

SECTION G. Drainage: The park shall be located on a well-drained and properly graded site. Necessary site drainage improvements as approved hy the Town shail be provided.

SECTION H: Interior Brives and Walkweys - All mobile home spaces shall abut upon an interiar paved drive of no less than twenty (20) feet in width, which shall have unobstructed access to a public street or highway in accordance with Ordinances of the Town. Hard surface walkways on less than three (3) feet wide

Off-Drive Parking- Each mobile home space shail be provided with at least one {1} off-drive parking space, dust-free and adequately marked. In addition, the developer shall provide one (1) additionsi off-drive parking space, dust-free and adequately marked for each three (3) mobile home spaces in the park.

Signs- The following non-flashing and non-animated sighs are permitted under the conditions specified:

- 1. Park Identification Sign - One (1) park identification sign shail be permitted not to exceed twenty-four (24) square feet in area for the purpase af denating the name of the Mobile Home Park.

- 2. Mobile Home Identification Sign - One (1) mobile home identification Siqn not exceeding one (1) square foot in area shall be permitted for each mobile home. Said sign Shall indicate only the name and address of the occupant of the mobile home.

- 3. No sign shall he located sa as to impede vehicular visibility at any intersection of the street Lines with one another or the edge of driveways with street lines.

Improvements to Mobile Homes

- 1. No permanent addition of any Rind shall be built into or become 4a part of any mobile home with the exception of awnings, porches and provided 311 mobile homes must he on permanent foundations which are concealed from sight by the use of landscaping, skirting, fencing, painting or other appropriate means.

- 2. The owner of s Mobile Home Park shal! provide a concrete patio of at least Four (4} inches thick on the access Side af the mobile home so as to lie beneath both doors, provided, however, said patio shall be a minimum of elagnt (8) feet in width and &@ minimum of forty (40) feet in length.

Special Conditions and Ssfequards- In recommending any planned Mobile Home Park, the Mayor and Council may attach special conditions and safeguards to protect both the occupants of the park and the occupants of surrounding property, including such matters as protection against noise, lights, dust and fire. Wherever there is not a public fire hydrant within 1,000 feet of each mobile home space, as measured along the roadways, thd Mobile Home Park shall be provided with hydrants for flre use within 20 feet of each mobile home space, equipped for use With standard garden hose.

General Requirements.

- 1. Hinimum Size of Mobile Homes - No mobile home shall he placed in a planned Mobile Home Park which has less than 500 square feet of Floor space and does nat contain a built-in bathroom with water closet, lavatory and shower or tub which are in working condition.

- 2. Water, Sewage and Electricity- Each mobile home space shall be provided with and each home connected to a central sanitary sewerage and water supply system approved by the County Health Officer. Electrical outlets shall he provided a5 specified by the County Building or Electrical Inspector.

- 3. Lighting - All interior drives and walkways within the park shall he lighted at night with electric Lamps Spaced at intervals af no more than 160 feet; oar equivalent lighting a5 approved by the County.

- 4. Refuse Collecting Facilities - Individual, water tight, covered refuse containers of not less than 10 gallon nor more than 20 gallon capacity shall be provided at each occupied mobile home space, and stands must be provided to hold the refuse containers upright or buried.

Collection service at least twice weekly shali be provided and disposal shall he as spproved by the Health Officer.

- 5. Recreation Area- At least five (5) percent of the gross area shali be set aside for recreational use. If a swimming pool is provided it may be counted as part of the area alloted for recreational use, and such pool Must be constructed in accordance with standards recommended by the Georgia Department of Public Health.

Existing Parks and Individual Mobile Homes - Ail existing Mobile Home Parks and individual mobile homes in the town at the time of adoption of this Ordinance are required to comply with the following regulations:

- 1. Existing Mobite Homes - Mobile homes Located oan individual lots when this Ordinance becomes effective shall be permitted, provided thet if any mobile home is Moved it must be relocated in a Mobile Home Park and no new mobile home shali take its place.

- 2. Mobile homes, not including travel trailers, may be Stored only in Mobile Home Parks and mobile home sales lots or within the confines of a building (warehouse).

SECTION Q: Development Compiiance - At least twenty (20) spaces of a Planned Mobile Home Park must be completely constructed, according to the Mobile Home Park Plan approved by the Mayor and Council within two (2) years after such approval by the Council. The failure of the developer or applicant to construct this minimum phase compietely within the specified period of time may be cause for the Mayor and Council to reconsider the planned Mobile Home Park.

- 1. Any person violating any provision of this Ordinance shall be guiity of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction shall be punished for each affense by a fine not exceeding one hundred fifty ($150.00) dollars or hy imprisonment not to exceed Fifty (50) days. Each day such violation continues shall he deemed 3 Separate offense. At the discretion of the Circuit Judge, a violation of this Ordinance may be given a reasonable length of time to rectify or correct the violation.

- 2. Separability of Provisions - Should any section or provision of this Ordinance be declared invalid, such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portion of this Ordinance.

Conflict with Other Regulations- Whenever the regulations of this Ordinance require @ greater width or sige of the yards, courts or other open space,or impose other restrictive standards than are required in or under any other statutes, the regulations and requirements of this Ordinance shall govern. Whenever the provisions of any other Georgia or Harris County statute require more restrictive standards than are required by this Ordinance, the provisions of such statute shall govern.
